shared_evidence.source: YouTube Help: audience retention/key moments and performance FAQ
shared_evidence.summary: YouTube retention analysis emphasizes intros, top moments, spikes and dips, and comparison against videos of similar length. Recommendation/search guidance says performance and relevance matter and warns against relying on myths or one-off changes.

shared_evidence.source: YouTube Help: Test & Compare thumbnails and YouTube Analytics API metrics
shared_evidence.summary: YouTube supports controlled thumbnail comparison using watch-time share and exposes averageViewDuration, averageViewPercentage and retention-related metrics. Creative learning should use comparable videos and observed analytics rather than fixed universal retention numbers.

shared_evidence.source: LangGraph official persistence, interrupts, functional API and fault-tolerance documentation
shared_evidence.summary: Durable execution uses checkpoints and thread IDs; successful node writes can survive sibling failure; replay resumes from checkpoints; task results should be serializable; external side effects should be idempotent; retries should be class-specific and bounded.

shared_evidence.source: Anthropic Engineering: Effective harnesses for long-running agents and Harness design for long-running application development
shared_evidence.summary: Long-running agents benefit from incremental work, structured progress artifacts, explicit acceptance criteria, clean handoffs, verification before marking done, and durable state across context resets. Overly broad one-shot execution and premature completion are recurring failure modes.

shared_evidence.source: GitHub Actions official docs: dependency caching, artifacts, reruns, concurrency
shared_evidence.summary: Caches are accelerators for regenerable data, while artifacts preserve produced outputs across jobs/runs. Failed jobs can be rerun, concurrency must be controlled, and cache hits are not proof of durable checkpoint correctness.
FFmpeg concat/segment primitives and ffprobe machine-readable stream inspection support scene/chapter-first rendering, contract checks, deterministic joining, and validation before final delivery.

The current system already has atomic scene promotion, content-addressed manifests, bounded retries, scene media contracts, predownload/decode validation, subprocess timeouts, Scene -> Validate -> Checkpoint -> Join, and final ffprobe/decode gates. The review must improve gaps without duplicating these rules.

Future normal news/topic explainers should target roughly 8-12 minutes without padding with irrelevant history or filler. User also requested stronger long-form know-how research and explicit measures that keep AI production from stopping, followed by peer review, durable storage and post-save verification.
